Never hand-edit; regenerate with npm run generate-catalog.

games.description: A walkable, 58-room New England harbor town built on FeltOS, carried live by QwzSpace, and rendered as a calm TUFTE interface. Exits, neighbors, evidence, weather, and exact-name commands all come from the same persistent world.

entryPoints.headless: POST /connect, POST /command, POST /tick, GET /events?actor=, GET /metrics (JSON-over-HTTP), plus QwzSpace WebSocket at /

games.statusNote: The harbor sleeps between visits and catches up in bounded steps on requests; every settled mutation is flushed to persistent storage.

games.description: A browser 3D fantasy MMORPG built on QwzSpace: a hand-rolled RFC 6455 WebSocket server running a 15Hz tick loop, with real combat, claim altars, an illocutionary speech-act system (assert/deny/abstain/contest), marks, K4-gauge powers, and an economy, over a four-valued bilattice world-truth model.
games.statusNote: Known limitation: marks and inventory mutate state directly and do not survive a restore. (Event-log compaction and the sustained-traffic OOM crash-loop this used to note were fixed and verified live 2026-08-20 -- see the deploy runbook's Known open issues.)

games.description: An LLM-native MUD: a tidal shore built on current FeltOS, transported by qwzspace rooms, wired to a fully agent-legible perception-frame protocol -- agents and humans as first-class players alike. 15 rooms across shore/pool/underwater registers, tide-gated diving, ecology harvesting, trade, governance, and two honest FOUR-valued contradictions that age toward settlement.

entryPoints.agent: WS upgrade at / speaking tidepool.protocol.v1 -- see docs/PROTOCOL.md; npm run bot runs the reference agent player

games.statusNote: The world is request-driven, not timer-driven (design: catch-up-on-request, not setInterval) -- it only advances when an HTTP request or a WS connection visits, per the deploy runbook's landed persistence pattern. A deployment with no other traffic needs SOME periodic visitor (a Cloud Run health probe, real users, or the reference bot's own documented health-check nudge) to keep ticking; this is intentional ("the harbor sleeps between visitors"), not a bug. Deploy with --no-cpu-throttling if health-probe-only traffic must still tick promptly, matching Farstone's own documented Cloud Run caveat.
